full_query: A 45-year-old man presents to a physician due to difficulty swallowing and slurred speech. For the past 3 months, the patient has been coughing when he drinks liquids. His speech also sounds different according to his wife. The patient has no significant medical history. His temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 110/80 mmHg, pulse is 60/min, and respirations are 12/min. On physical exam, he is unable to fully extend his tongue, and there are fasciculations on his tongue. When tapping the mandible at the chin while the mouth is held open, there is pronounced upward movement of the lower jaw. Sensory exam reveals no deficits. Which of the following therapies is most likely to improve survival for this patient's disease process? (A) Baclofen (B) Dextromethorphan and quinidine (C) Edaravone (D) Riluzole (E) Tizanidine

shared_context.exam_findings: unable to fully extend tongue, tongue fasciculations, pronounced upward movement of lower jaw upon mandible tapping, no sensory deficits

sentences: To determine the best answer, let's analyze the patient's symptoms and physical exam findings
The patient's difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and slurred speech may indicate a neuromuscular disorder
The patient's past coughing when drinking liquids and slurred speech suggest that the patient may have a disorder of the central or peripheral nervous system, as these symptoms can lead to aspiration
The patient has no significant medical history, which makes it less likely that the symptoms are due to a secondary cause, such as a medication side effect or another medical condition
The lack of fever, normal blood pressure, and normal pulse and respirations make an infectious or acute inflammatory cause less likely

The physical exam findings of inability to fully extend the tongue, fasciculations on the tongue, and pronounced upward movement of the lower jaw when tapping the mandible suggest a disorder of the lower motor neuron
The sensory exam reveals no deficits, which further supports a lower motor neuron disorder
Based on these findings, the most likely diagnosis is amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a motor neuron disease characterized by the progressive degeneration of both upper and lower motor neurons

Given the diagnosis of ALS, the best therapy for improving survival would be Riluzole, which is the only FDA-approved medication forALS and has been shown to prolong survival by an average of 2-3 months
